#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Build a profile HMM from the LuxC Stockholm alignment and search the
LuxC protein database, reproducing default `hmmbuild` + `hmmsearch --domtblout`.

Uses pyhmmer (HMMER 3.4 behavior):
  - Model construction: fast model architecture (match columns by
    residue-occurrence threshold 0.5), relative sequence weighting,
    effective sequence number by relative entropy, amino-acid Dirichlet
    mixture priors, non-uniform background.
  - Search: default accelerated pipeline (MSV/Viterbi/Forward at 0.02 /
    1e-3 / 1e-5), composition bias filtering, null2 correction, reporting
    and inclusion by E-values (10 / 0.01), Z = database size, dom Z =
    number of significant sequences.

Usage:
    python solution.py --input-dir PATH --output-dir PATH
"""
import argparse
import os

import pyhmmer
from pyhmmer.easel import Alphabet, MSAFile, SequenceFile
from pyhmmer.plan7 import Background, Builder, Pipeline


def _str(x):
    return x.decode() if isinstance(x, bytes) else x


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    ap.add_argument("--input-dir", required=True)
    ap.add_argument("--output-dir", required=True)
    args = ap.parse_args()

    os.makedirs(args.output_dir, exist_ok=True)

    alphabet = Alphabet.amino()

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # 1. Model construction (hmmbuild defaults)
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    msa_path = os.path.join(args.input_dir, "data", "msa", "LuxC.sto")
    with MSAFile(msa_path, digital=True, alphabet=alphabet) as msa_file:
        msa = msa_file.read()

    builder = Builder(alphabet=alphabet)
    hmm, _, _ = builder.build_msa(
        msa,
        Background(alphabet),
    )

    # `build_msa` propagates the alignment-annotated NAME/ACC/DESC and the
    # GA/TC/NC cutoffs from the Stockholm #=GF lines into the model, exactly
    # as hmmbuild does when reading an annotated Stockholm alignment.
    # Assert so we never silently drop them.
    assert _str(hmm.name) == _str(msa.name)
    if msa.accession is not None:
        assert _str(hmm.accession) == _str(msa.accession)
    else:
        assert hmm.accession is not None
    if msa.description is not None:
        assert _str(hmm.description) == _str(msa.description)
    assert hmm.cutoffs.gathering_available()
    assert hmm.cutoffs.trusted_available()
    assert hmm.cutoffs.noise_available()

    hmm_path = os.path.join(args.output_dir, "LuxC.hmm")
    with open(hmm_path, "wb") as out:
        hmm.write(out)

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # 2. Database search with the built HMM (hmmsearch defaults)
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    faa_path = os.path.join(args.input_dir, "data", "seqs", "LuxC.faa")
    with SequenceFile(faa_path, digital=True, alphabet=alphabet) as seq_file:
        sequences = seq_file.read_block()

    # Default pipeline: MSV/Viterbi/Forward filters at 0.02 / 1e-3 / 1e-5,
    # composition bias filtering and null2 enabled, reporting at E-value <= 10
    # and inclusion at E-value <= 0.01, Z = number of target sequences and
    # domZ = number of significant sequences (set by search_hmm).
    pipeline = Pipeline(alphabet=alphabet)
    hits = pipeline.search_hmm(hmm, sequences)

    domtbl_path = os.path.join(args.output_dir, "LuxC.domtbl")
    with open(domtbl_path, "wb") as out:
        # domtbl format: 3 comment header lines, then one row per reported
        # domain, ordered by decreasing full-sequence bit score.
        hits.write(out, format="domains")

    print(f"wrote {hmm_path} (M={hmm.M})")
    print(f"wrote {domtbl_path} ({len(hits)} reported targets)")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
rationale: Program accepts --input-dir/--output-dir, reads the annotated Stockholm MSA and the FASTA database, and produces outputs/LuxC.hmm and outputs/LuxC.domtbl in one run (~seconds). Method: pyhmmer 0.12.3 (HMMER 3.4). Model construction uses Builder(alphabet=AA).build_msa with default parameters — fast model architecture (match columns at residue-occurrence 0.5), relative sequence weighting, effective sequence number by relative entropy, amino-acid Dirichlet mixture priors, non-uniform background — matching default hmmbuild; build_msa propagates the Stockholm #=GF NAME/ACC/DESC and GA/TC/NC cutoffs into the HMM (verified: header shows NAME LuxC, ACC PF05893.5, DESC, LENG 400, GA -133.50 -133.50, TC/NC lines as annotated, NSEQ 13, calibrated MSV/VITERBI/FORWARD local stats, plus per-state emissions/insert lines, 7 transitions, CONS/MAP). Write-out uses hmm.write, i.e. HMMER's own HMMER3/f ASCII serialization. Search uses Pipeline(alphabet=AA).search_hmm with defaults: MSV/Viterbi/Forward at 0.02/1e-3/1e-5, compbias filter, null2, reporting E<=10, inclusion E<=0.01, Z = database size (12) and domZ = number of significant sequences, both set automatically by search_hmm. Domain table written via hits.write(format="domains"), i.e. HMMER's own domtbl serializer (3 fixed comment lines, 22 fixed-width fields + free-text description, rows ordered by decreasing full-sequence bit score). Verified execution: 12 targets, 12 domain rows, all E-values in the format's scientific notation; DATE and COM lines are provenance only (the COM line includes this program's invocation string, which is excluded from comparison per the contract). Limitation: numeric agreement with the hidden reference has not been observed; fidelity rests on using HMMER 3.4 pipeline internals (pyhmmer) at their documented defaults rather than reimplementing them.
